qmroot_binding.note: 6D absent; negative rungs absent; INV-013 = 0D only

description: Defines the structural model of pattern mutation and propagation. Mutation is the change of a pattern's configuration while retaining at least one invariant from its source invariant set (INV-PD-003). Propagation is the transport of a pattern to a new structural context such that the propagated instance is detectable by Book 3 methods (INV-PD-004). This map covers mutation anchor identification, dissolution conditions, propagation validity, signature fidelity, and the cross-book propagation instances that constitute the primary empirical content of Book 9.

anchor_definition.label: Mutation Anchor
anchor_definition.description: The non-empty intersection invariant_set(P') ∩ invariant_set(P). The mutation anchor is the structural continuity thread that licenses P' as a mutation of P rather than a new pattern. PD-Μ must identify and record the anchor before classifying any transition as a mutation.
anchor_definition.anchor_quality: Anchors with more invariants in common represent stronger mutations — the pattern retains more of its structural identity. Anchors with exactly one invariant are minimal mutations and receive an elevated drift cost in PD-Μ evaluation.

dissolution_condition.label: Structural Dissolution
dissolution_condition.description: Total invariant loss — a transition producing P' with invariant_set(P') ∩ invariant_set(P) = ∅ — is structural dissolution, not mutation. Dissolution must be logged as a terminal trajectory event by PD-Μ and forwarded to PD-Τ for trajectory closure.
dissolution_condition.pd_action: PD-Μ logs the dissolution event with: (a) the final valid configuration P, (b) the attempted successor P', (c) the full invariant_set comparison showing empty intersection, (d) the trajectory time-point t_dissolution. The dissolution event is forwarded to the catalogue phase.
dissolution_condition.dissolution_vs_bifurcation: If the dissolving pattern P has a mutation anchor in a parallel trajectory continuation (a surviving branch from a prior bifurcation event), the dissolution is reclassified as a selective dissolution — the anchor invariants survive in the parallel branch and PD-Μ reclassifies the event as a cross-branch mutation.

mutation_types.label: Conservative Mutation
mutation_types.description: A mutation in which P' preserves all invariants of P except exactly one, which is weakened or replaced. The anchor contains all but one of P's invariants. The pattern changes minimally — maximum structural continuity.
cross_book_instances: GRL regime topology shift: RT-001 (Hierarchical) → RT-002 (Inverted-Star) preserving all regime constraints except the centralization constraint — conservative mutation of the regime pattern
NoS realism position shift: ESR → OSR preserving structural fallibilism (DC-003) while replacing the intrinsic-nature assumption — conservative mutation of the structural realism pattern

mutation_types.label: Standard Mutation
mutation_types.description: A mutation in which P' preserves at least two invariants of P but loses one or more. The anchor is a proper non-trivial subset of invariant_set(P). Standard case.
cross_book_instances: SARG argument mutation: argument A mutates under partial defeat — some invariants lost (INV-SARG-003 defeat events), root reachability preserved (INV-SARG-001 anchor), warrant structure partially preserved (INV-SARG-002 anchor)
OR revelation pattern: partial revelation mutation — opacity measurement invariants preserved (INV-OR-001, INV-OR-003) while revelation threshold condition changes (INV-OR-002 lost)

mutation_types.label: Minimal Mutation
mutation_types.description: A mutation in which exactly one invariant is shared between P and P'. Minimal anchor. High structural divergence — P and P' share only a single structural commitment. PD-Μ flags minimal mutations for elevated review by PD-Σ.
cross_book_instances: NoS-to-PD identity boundary: a meta-structural pattern retaining only INV-NOS-001 (Structural Autonomy) while all other NoS invariants are revised — minimal mutation at the capstone boundary

TEL expression mutation: a TEL composition pattern retaining only INV-TEL-001 (Expression Completeness) while compositionality and semantic stability invariants are revised under a new grammar extension

mutation_types.label: Chain Mutation
mutation_types.description: A sequence of mutations P → P' → P'' → ... in which each adjacent pair satisfies the mutation validity condition (anchor ≠ ∅) but transitivity is not applied — P'' need not share an invariant with P directly. Chain mutations are valid at each step; the chain does not guarantee overall identity between the chain origin and terminus.
mutation_types.chain_drift_accumulation: Each link in a chain mutation accumulates the drift cost of its mutation type. PD-Μ tracks cumulative chain drift and flags chains exceeding a total drift threshold of 0.20 for PD-Σ synthesis review.
mutation_types.pd_note: Chain mutations are the primary mechanism by which long-range pattern evolution is modeled in Book 9. They permit structural change over many steps without requiring any single step to violate INV-PD-003.

propagation_model.title: Structural Propagation Model
propagation_model.formal: propagation_valid(P, P', C') ⟺ ∃m ∈ SD_methods: m(C') identifies P' as a structural signature matching sig(P)  [INV-PD-004]

signature_model.definition: sig(P) = the structural signature of pattern P — the set of relational features that make P uniquely identifiable by Book 3 detection methods (INV-SD-001 Signature Uniqueness)
components: Invariant fingerprint: the ordered list of invariant IDs satisfied by P
Relational profile: the distribution of relation types in R_P
Cross-book tags: which upstream book vocabularies contributed to P's structural definition
signature_model.signature_matching: sig(P') ≅ sig(P) ⟺ sig(P') satisfies the INV-SD-001 uniqueness condition relative to P — the signature is specific enough to uniquely identify P in C'

detection_method_requirement.description: At least one Book 3 structural detection method must be applicable to the target context C'. If C' is too opaque for any SD method to operate (opacity level ω(C') ≥ δ for all available observers — INV-OR-002 violation), the propagation claim cannot be verified and is suspended pending opacity reduction.
detection_method_requirement.opacity_gate: If ω(C') ≥ δ(O) for all O: propagation claim is suspended. PD-Π records the suspension with the blocking opacity level. Claim may be resubmitted after OR-Ω measurement confirms ω(C') has decreased below δ threshold.

detection_methods_available.label: Direct Signature Match
detection_methods_available.description: Apply the full sig(P) fingerprint to C' — all components match

detection_methods_available.label: Invariant Subset Match
detection_methods_available.description: Match on invariant fingerprint only — used when full signature is not computable in C'

detection_methods_available.label: Relational Profile Match
detection_methods_available.description: Match on relational profile — used when invariant computation is blocked by opacity

detection_methods_available.label: Cross-Book Tag Match
detection_methods_available.description: Match on cross-book provenance tags — weakest detection method; requires PD-Σ review before propagation is confirmed

propagation_types.label: Faithful Propagation
propagation_types.description: The propagated instance P' in C' satisfies the full signature match sig(P') = sig(P). Maximum propagation fidelity. P has reproduced its complete structural signature in the new context.
cross_book_instances: TEL expression propagation: a TEL composition pattern P propagates to a new structural domain C' while maintaining all grammar rule compliance — sig(P) fully preserved in the TEL encoding of P'
FFT structural identity propagation: a Book 1 primitive structural pattern propagates to a higher-level analysis context with full constraint and invariant set preserved

propagation_types.label: Degraded Propagation
propagation_types.description: The propagated instance P' in C' satisfies a partial signature match — the detectable portion of sig(P') covers the mutation anchor of INV-PD-003. Propagation is valid under combined INV-PD-003 and INV-PD-004 conditions: the signature degradation must not exceed the mutation constraint.
propagation_types.formal: degraded_propagation_valid(P, P', C') ⟺ sig(P') ∩ sig(P) ≠ ∅ ∧ invariant_set(P') ∩ invariant_set(P) ≠ ∅
cross_book_instances: GRL regime propagation: a regime pattern P propagates to a new institutional context C' — governance constraints partially degraded but authority decay model (INV-GRL-002) signature preserved
SARG argument propagation: an argument structure propagates to a new domain — warrant types change but root reachability (INV-SARG-001) and invariant anchor preserved

propagation_types.label: Latent Propagation
propagation_types.description: The propagated instance P' in C' is not immediately detectable by current SD methods but is predicted to become detectable once opacity in C' decreases below the revelation threshold. PD-Π suspends the propagation claim and schedules a re-detection query for when ω(C') < δ.
propagation_types.opacity_dependency: Requires ω(C') ≥ δ(O) — the propagation is latent due to context opacity, not pattern absence
propagation_types.cross_book_binding: INV-OR-003 (Opacity Persistence) and INV-OR-004 (Partial Revelation): the pattern may be partially visible through partial revelation
propagation_types.pd_action: PD-Π records the latent propagation claim with current ω(C') value. A re-detection trigger is registered: when PD-Τ receives an OR-Ω measurement update showing ω(C') < δ, PD-Π is reactivated to verify the propagation.

propagation_failure_modes.label: Signature Collapse
propagation_failure_modes.description: The propagated P' in C' has no detectable structural signature — sig(P') is empty relative to all SD detection methods. The propagation claim is invalid.
propagation_failure_modes.pd_action: PD-Π invalidates the propagation claim and reclassifies the event as a dissolution event. PD-Μ is notified to apply INV-PD-003 evaluation.

propagation_failure_modes.label: Context Incompatibility
propagation_failure_modes.description: The target context C' lacks the structural primitives required to instantiate any configuration with sig(P). The propagation is structurally impossible — not blocked by opacity but by structural incompatibility.
propagation_failure_modes.pd_action: PD-Π logs the context incompatibility with a structural analysis of what C' is missing. This is distinct from opacity blocking (PFM-003) — the issue is ontological, not epistemic.
propagation_failure_modes.cross_book_note: Context incompatibility often arises when propagation is attempted across incompatible tier levels without the required dependency modules loaded.

propagation_failure_modes.label: Opacity Blocking
propagation_failure_modes.description: ω(C') ≥ δ(O) for all available observers — no SD method can operate in C'. Propagation cannot be verified. Claim is suspended (not invalidated).
propagation_failure_modes.pd_action: See latent propagation (PT-003). This is a suspension, not a failure — the claim may be verified once opacity decreases.
propagation_failure_modes.resolution: OR-Ω re-measurement of ω(C') followed by PD-Π reactivation

propagation_failure_modes.label: Anchor Violation in Transit
propagation_failure_modes.description: During propagation transit — the transformation sequence that moves P from its source context to C' — the mutation constraint (INV-PD-003) is violated. The arriving P' has no anchor invariant shared with P. The propagation is invalid even if P' is detectable in C'.
propagation_failure_modes.pd_action: PD-Μ is consulted to verify the mutation chain from P to P'. If the transit violates INV-PD-003 at any step, the propagation is reclassified as a dissolution event at the step of anchor loss, followed by the emergence of a new unrelated pattern P' in C'.

cross_book_propagation_instances.description: Regime patterns propagate when a governance structure is replicated in a new institutional context. The regime tuple R = ⟨N_R, E_R, C_R, S_R, α_R, λ_R⟩ is the source pattern. Propagation fidelity requires that the authority decay model (INV-GRL-002 signature) is detectable in the new context.
cross_book_propagation_instances.pd_operators: PD-Μ (mutation check on constraint set changes) + PD-Π (signature detection in new context via SDM-002)

cross_book_propagation_instances.description: SARG argument patterns propagate when a structural argumentation form is reused across domains. The argument tuple A = ⟨N_A, R_A, C_A, root(A)⟩ is the source pattern. Propagation fidelity requires that the reachability structure (INV-SARG-001 signature) is detectable in the new domain.
cross_book_propagation_instances.pd_operators: PD-Μ (mutation check on node and relation type changes) + PD-Π (signature detection via SDM-002 or SDM-003)

cross_book_propagation_instances.description: NoS patterns propagate when a meta-structural commitment (e.g., the OSR structural realism pattern) is instantiated across different structural levels. Propagation fidelity requires that INV-NOS-001 (Structural Autonomy) is detectable in the target structural level — the dominant cross-level propagation anchor.
cross_book_propagation_instances.pd_operators: PD-Μ (INV-NOS-003 identity check as mutation anchor) + PD-Π (INV-NOS-001 signature detection across levels)
